title: "Mouse hypothalamus (MERFISH)"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", cache = TRUE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5.5)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = "/mnt/c/Users/tingthou/Desktop/SIGNAL/SingleCell/RealData")
```

This page analyses single-cell MERFISH data of the preoptic area of the mouse
hypothalamus (Moffitt *et al.*, 2018) with cell-type labels and a single
Gaussian spatial kernel. To keep the page quick, it runs three genes named in
the paper; the analysis of all 155 genes uses the same code.

## Data

The processed data used on this page, `Mouse_hypothalamic_preoptic.Rdata`,
can be downloaded from the
[SIGNAL real data folder](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-j6l-KBT9dR_p2RB2RVb_5q9Ig2GdRn3)
on Google Drive. The data come from the BASS analysis page
(<https://zhengli09.github.io/BASS-Analysis/MERFISH.html>): the tissue section
at Bregma −0.09 mm from animal 1, with 155 genes on 5,557 cells.

```{r load}
library(SIGNAL)
library(Matrix)
load("Mouse_hypothalamic_preoptic.Rdata")
dim(data_use$count_use)
table(data_use$cluster)
```

The 37 pericytes are too few for per-cell-type testing and are removed,
leaving 5,520 cells in eight cell types:

```{r subset}
keep     <- data_use$cluster != "Pericytes"
counts   <- data_use$count_use[, keep]
location <- data_use$location_coord[keep, ]
celltype <- droplevels(factor(data_use$cluster[keep]))
```

## Step 1: create a SIGNAL object

Three genes from the paper: *Gad1*, a marker of inhibitory neurons; *Cck*,
expressed in one region of the tissue across several cell types; and *Gda*,
with different spatial patterns in inhibitory and excitatory neurons.

```{r create}
genes <- c("Gad1", "Cck", "Gda")
obj <- createSIGNALobject(counts[genes, ], location, celltype)
obj
```

## Step 2: filter and transform

```{r preprocess}
obj <- SIGNAL_preprocess(obj, min_cells = 0, seed = 1)
```

## Step 3: build the kernels

The cell-type input is a vector of labels, so SIGNAL uses the Hamming
cell-type kernel. As in CELINA's approximation mode, we use one Gaussian
spatial kernel (`approximation = TRUE`). Its bandwidth is chosen from the
expression of **all** genes with Silverman's rule; with only three genes in
the object, we compute it from the full count matrix and pass it on:

```{r kernel}
bw <- select_bandwidth(counts)
bw
obj <- SIGNAL_kernel(obj, approximation = TRUE, bandwidth = bw)
names(obj@spatial_kernels)
```

## Step 4: test the genes

```{r test}
obj <- SIGNAL_test(obj, ncores = 3, verbose = FALSE)
signif(obj@result, 3)
```

All three genes are detected by the overall test. Values of about 1e-16 are
below the accuracy of Davies' method (about 1e-6); use
`method = "saddlepoint"` to keep their actual size.

```{r classify}
res <- obj@result
apply(res[, c("p_celltype", "p_spatial", "p_ctSVG")] < 0.05, 1, function(f)
  paste(c("CellType", "Spatial", "ctSVG")[f], collapse = "+"))
```

## Step 5: visualise the genes

```{r plot-gad1}
SIGNAL_plotGene(obj, "Gad1", by_celltype = TRUE, point_size = 0.4)
```

```{r plot-cck}
SIGNAL_plotGene(obj, "Cck", by_celltype = TRUE, point_size = 0.4)
```

```{r plot-gda}
SIGNAL_plotGene(obj, "Gda", by_celltype = TRUE, point_size = 0.4)
```

## Step 6: cell types behind the cell-type-specific pattern

```{r celltype}
obj <- SIGNAL_celltype(obj, genes = "Gda", ncores = 3, verbose = FALSE)
signif(obj@celltype_result, 2)
```
